This notebook does not download anything. Run `main.r` first, then this file only reads what
`main.r` saved in `output/` and shows it.

# 0. libraries

```{r packages}
# the notebook is one folder down, so the renv library is loaded from the project folder
if (file.exists("../renv/activate.R")) renv::load("..")

source(here::here("Scripts", "setup.r"))
source(here::here("Scripts", "areas.r"))
source(here::here("Scripts", "embeddings.r"))
source(here::here("Scripts", "download.r"))
library(mapview)
```

# 1. values

Same values as in `main.r`.

```{r setup}
run_mode <- "boxes"
years <- c(2021, 2022, 2023)
embeddings <- c("alphaEarth", "tessera")
target_crs <- "EPSG:25832"
pixel_size <- 10
tile_size <- 10000

# FALSE = leave out the piles of overlapping boxes (I found some groups major ones near: Hachenburg, Kelheim, Eberswalde)
# TRUE = keep all boxes
overlap_boxes <- FALSE

tessera_ver <- "v1.1"
aef_https <- "https://data.source.coop/tge-labs/aef/v1/annual"
aef_index_file <- "aef_index.gpkg"

grid_dir <- here::here("output", "grid")
cache_dir <- here::here("data", "cache")
if (run_mode == "boxes") {
  out_root <- here::here("output", "boxes")
} else {
  out_root <- here::here("output", "tiles")
}
```

# 2. Area of Interest: Germany + buffer zone

```{r AOI}
DE <- st_read(file.path(grid_dir, "germany.gpkg"), quiet = TRUE)
DE_buf <- st_read(file.path(grid_dir, "aoi.gpkg"), quiet = TRUE)

buffer_plot(DE, DE_buf)

cat(
  "Area of DE without buffer: ", sum(as.numeric(st_area(DE))) / 1e6, " km²\n",
  "Area of DE with buffer: ", sum(as.numeric(st_area(DE_buf))) / 1e6, " km²\n",
  sep = ""
)
```

# 3. BOXES for BWI

One box per cluster region. All rows of the same cluster name belong to the same region, so we
make one box around all of them.

```{r boxes}
boxes <- st_read(file.path(grid_dir, "cluster_boxes.gpkg"), quiet = TRUE)
dropped_boxes <- st_read(file.path(grid_dir, "dropped_boxes.gpkg"), quiet = TRUE)

all_boxes <- rbind(boxes, dropped_boxes)
if (overlap_boxes) {
  boxes <- all_boxes
} else {
  boxes <- all_boxes[all_boxes$group_size < 3, ]
}

print(nrow(boxes))
print(nrow(dropped_boxes))

# 1 = no overlap, 2 = two boxes overlap each other
table(boxes$group_size)
```

### Overlapping boxes

Near Hachenburg, Kelheim and Eberswalde many boxes lie on top of each other, so `main.r` leaves out every
box that is in a group of 3 or more overlapping boxes.

```{r dropped}
# where the dropped groups are
centres <- st_coordinates(st_transform(st_centroid(st_geometry(dropped_boxes)), 4326))
dropped_boxes$lon <- centres[, 1]
dropped_boxes$lat <- centres[, 2]

dropped_boxes %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  group_by(overlap_group) %>%
  summarise(n_boxes = n(), lon = round(mean(lon), 2), lat = round(mean(lat), 2),
            names_7_digits = sum(cluster_name >= 1000000))

# the pairs we keep, and their longitude
pairs <- boxes[boxes$group_size == 2, ]
summary(st_coordinates(st_transform(st_centroid(st_geometry(pairs)), 4326))[, 1])
```

```{r overlap_map}
# red = left out, blue = pairs we keep
mapview(dropped_boxes, col.regions = "red") + mapview(pairs, col.regions = "blue")
```

# 4. The 10 x 10 km tiles for us

Each tile starts at a multiple of 10 km, so every tile edge is also on our 10 m grid.

```{r tiles}
tiles <- st_read(file.path(grid_dir, "tiles_10km.gpkg"), quiet = TRUE)
print(nrow(tiles))

# just to view all the tiles and the boxes
mapview(tiles) + mapview(boxes)
```

# 5. Why no fixed grid for the cluster boxes

```{r grid_test}
# how many boxes are cut by a fixed grid of different sizes
sizes_km <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100, 150, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800)
grid_test <- data.frame(size_km = sizes_km, boxes_cut = NA)
for (i in 1:nrow(grid_test)) {
  grid_test$boxes_cut[i] <- count_cut_boxes(boxes, grid_test$size_km[i] * 1000)
  print(grid_test[i, ])
}

plot(grid_test$size_km, grid_test$boxes_cut + 1, log = "xy", type = "b", pch = 19,
     xlab = "tile size (km)", ylab = "cluster boxes cut",
     main = "how many boxes does it cut")
```

Every grid size keeps cutting the cluster boxes, until the grid is almost as big as Germany from
north to south (800 km). So we take one box for each cluster.

# 7. Alpha Earth

```{r aef_index}
aef_index <- get_aef_index(aef_https, aef_index_file, DE_buf, tile_size, target_crs, cache_dir)
print(table(aef_index$year))   # number of files per year in AOI
```

# 8. AEF speed

In the test run one AEF box took about 40 s and a 10 km tile 3 to 4 min. TESSERA took 2 to 7 s
for the same box.

If the AEF files say `INTERLEAVE=BAND`, each of the 64 bands is stored on its own. GDAL then
reads the box band after band, and every band waits for the server in the US (about 0.5 s).
64 x 0.5 s is about the 40 s we see. More GDAL settings did not change this in a test with a
slow local server, so the fix is to run several parts of `main.r` at the same time.

```{r aef_speed}
# how the AEF files are stored
one_file <- aef_index$url[aef_index$year == 2022][1]
info <- describe(one_file)
print(info[grepl("INTERLEAVE|Band 1 Block", info)])

# time for one box, the same way as in the download
b <- boxes[1, ]
template <- rast(ext(b$xmin, b$xmax, b$ymin, b$ymax), res = pixel_size, crs = target_crs)
start_time <- Sys.time()
x <- get_aef(template, 2022, aef_index)
print(as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), start_time, units = "secs")))
```

# 9. Checking files

```{r checker}
check_downloads(out_root, years, embeddings, pixel_size)
```

```{r times}
# seconds per download, from the time files of all parts
time_files <- list.files(out_root, pattern = "^download_times_part_.*csv$", full.names = TRUE)
times <- read_csv(time_files, show_col_types = FALSE)
times %>%
  group_by(embedding, year) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean_seconds = round(mean(seconds), 1), max_seconds = max(seconds))

# rough time for all areas in days, with 1 run and with 8 parts at the same time
if (run_mode == "boxes") {
  n_areas <- nrow(boxes)
} else {
  n_areas <- nrow(tiles)
}
sec_per_area <- sum(tapply(times$seconds, times$embedding, mean)) * length(years)
days <- sec_per_area * n_areas / 86400
print(round(c(one_run = days, eight_parts = days / 8), 1))
```
